review.verdict: NOT READY TO INTEGRATE AS-IS (contract-fidelity lens, L1). Behaviour was worked out by reading the code; nothing was run. The wire shapes in src/http-client.mjs and src/domain.mjs mostly match the real server at 79414143: endpoint paths and methods, payload field names, the status-token header, agreement pairs, pagination completeness and receipt shape all line up. Four contract gaps must still be fixed before this goes into the live staffed-ordering path. (1) The server refuses every submission that lacks a durable, server-recorded Early Access agreement on file and a live Early Access session. The package never reads or records that agreement, ManualOrderPage has no gate prop, and a 403 agreement_required leaves the customer stuck behind a locked form that says "Retry the same request" (P1). (2) Member mode sends a Bearer token on submit, which the existing client never does. The server then resolves a member viewer that needs a member-to-customer binding, so unbound members are refused (P2). (3) The server's error codes (validation_error with field/message, forbidden, agreement_required, 503) are collapsed into generic retry text (P2). (4) price_changed and catalog_changed lock the frozen request body. They are raised before the server's replay lookup, so the package's "Reload and review" advice can create a duplicate order after a response that was saved but lost in transit (P2). The 73 node and 18 browser checks the package claims to have passed are not verified here; its fake server never uses the real error codes.

findings.title: Server-recorded Early Access agreement is a hard precondition the package never satisfies; 403 agreement_required becomes a locked-form dead end
findings.claim: Every submit is refused unless the viewer has a live Early Access session with a customerRef and agreementGate.accepted(customerRef) is true. That acceptance is recorded only via the existing Research Use Policy read and POST /api/research/early-access/agreements/accept flow. The package does not read or record it, and ManualOrderPage has no continuation-gate prop. On the resulting 403 the package keeps the frozen request pending, locks the form and tells the customer to 'Retry the same request'. Every retry returns 403 again, and the only escape is a reload that loses everything entered. The server stays safe (no agreement bypass), but every customer without prior acceptance loses the request after filling in the whole form.
findings.evidence: Repo@79414143: service.ts:339-349 (refuses before validation) -> http.ts:163-167 (403 {error:'agreement_required'}); production-deps.ts:104-117 (needs earlyAccessSessionHash and customerRef, then agreementGate.accepted); client/src/research/adapters/earlyAccessAgreement.ts:17-19 (the accept endpoint the existing UI uses); EarlyAccessRoute.tsx:590 (the existing slot is gated continuationEnabled={agreed && blocked === null}); section.tsx:312 (the standalone route is ungated and depends on the server refusal, which AssistedOrderPage.tsx:778 maps to 'Review and accept the current Research Use Policy'). Package: ManualOrderPage.tsx:8-20 (no gate or standing prop) and :22 ('Mount inside the existing assisted-order route'); http-client.mjs:43-44 (403 becomes the generic 'Retry the same request or contact support', uncertain=false); order-form.mjs:257-265 (only 400/422 release pending, so 403 keeps the body frozen and labels the button 'Retry same request'); INTEGRATION.md never mentions the standing prerequisite.
findings.fix: Make the agreement on file an explicit precondition. Either accept a host-supplied gate (continuationEnabled, or a standing probe of GET /api/research/early-access/agreements) and refuse to render the submit step until it is satisfied, or route the customer to the existing policy and accept flow. Map 403 agreement_required to a specific instruction and release the frozen body, since nothing was saved. Document the prerequisite in INTEGRATION.md and add a test against the real 403 shape.

findings.title: Member mode sends a Bearer token on config, catalog and submit, unlike the existing client, so the server sees a different viewer and refuses unbound members
findings.claim: http-client attaches 'Authorization: Bearer <member token>' to every request, submit included. The existing client sends a member token only for owner reads and document calls; submit and catalog go cookie-only, so the server resolves an early_access_session viewer. With a Bearer, the server resolves a member viewer. That viewer carries Early Access standing only if the binding directory ties this member id to the session's customerRef; otherwise earlyAccessCustomerRef is null and the submit is refused with 403 agreement_required (then the L1-1 dead end). Pricing also switches from the Early Access retail grant to the member pricing viewer, and requests are attributed to the member instead of the session. The package therefore changes who can submit, at what price, and under which owner.
findings.evidence: Package: http-client.mjs:24 (Bearer whenever identity.token is set, for every request); ManualOrderPage.tsx:6-10. Repo@79414143: client/src/research/assisted-order/api.ts submitAssistedOrder and loadAssistedOrderCatalog (no Authorization header) vs requestOwnerHeaders (member token used only on status and documents); express.ts:95 (resolveMember reads the Bearer via requireActiveMember, server/index.ts:391-405), :120-146 (earlyAccessCustomerRef set only when identitiesBound); production-deps.ts:109-115; server/index.ts pricingViewerForCustomerViewer comment (Early Access retail grant vs member grant).
findings.fix: Match the existing client: send config, catalog and submit with cookies only, and keep the member Bearer for owner status reads. If member-attributed submission is a deliberate product change, it needs its own decision plus proof that bound and unbound members both get a truthful outcome.

findings.title: Server error vocabulary is discarded: validation_error field/message, forbidden and 503 collapse into generic retry text
findings.claim: The server returns 400 {error:'validation_error', field, message} with actionable messages, for example which line is no longer available or that a stale form acknowledgment needs a refresh. It returns 403 forbidden for an ended or absent session and 503 assisted_order_unavailable when the bridge is disabled. The package keeps only the error code and shows 'The request was not confirmed. Retry the same request or contact support.' for all of them. On 400 it changes the button to 'Submit corrected request' without saying what to correct. On 403 forbidden it keeps the body frozen and invites endless retries. During load, a catalog 503 can win the Promise.all race and show 'This information is not available. Please retry.' instead of the truthful 'Ordering is not available'. The existing wizard maps each of these codes to a specific instruction.
findings.evidence: Repo@79414143: http.ts:148-186 (shapes); service.ts:378-384 (line-scoped product refusal), :386-391 (quantity message), :1150-1166 (stale-form acknowledgment message); server/index.ts:858-869 (503 door); AssistedOrderPage.tsx:762-785 (existing per-code mapping including field highlight). Package: http-client.mjs:39-45 (payload.message and payload.field ignored; generic POST message); :71 (Promise.all of config and catalog); order-form.mjs:256-265.
findings.fix: Carry payload.field and the server's customer-safe message (or a mapped equivalent) into OrderError. Map validation_error to a field-specific message, forbidden to 'session ended, return to Early Access', agreement_required as in L1-1, and 503 to unavailable. Load config before the catalog, or prefer the config verdict. Add tests that use the real server shapes instead of 'database_unavailable'.

findings.title: price_changed/catalog_changed: the frozen body loops on 409, and 'Reload and review' can create a duplicate after a saved-but-lost first attempt
findings.claim: The server checks expected price, catalog version and price version before the idempotent createOrReplay. On a first attempt these 409s are definitive (nothing was saved), yet the package marks every 409 as uncertain and keeps the frozen body. 'Retry same request' then returns the same 409 forever, and there is no catalog-refresh path like the existing recoverFromDrift. In the compound case — the first POST was saved but its response was lost (network drop or the 20 s timeout), and the price or catalog version changes before the retry — the retry gets 409 price_changed instead of the replayed receipt. The package tells the customer to 'Reload and review the request'. A reload remounts the form with a new idempotency key, so the second submit creates a second request, and nothing warns that the first may already be saved. Severity is P2 because two events must coincide, but the outcome is a duplicate order.
findings.evidence: Repo@79414143: service.ts:393-420 (conflicts thrown) precede service.ts:495 (createOrReplay); AssistedOrderPage.tsx:687,764-767 (existing recoverFromDrift refreshes selections). Package: http-client.mjs:41 (message 'A price changed. Reload and review the request.'), :44 (uncertain=true for every 409); order-form.mjs:257-265 (409 keeps pending), :10-11,243 (attemptKey regenerated only on remount); http-client.mjs:29 (20 s AbortSignal.timeout).
findings.fix: Track whether this attempt has ever had an uncertain outcome. If it has, show price_changed/catalog_changed as 'Your earlier attempt may already be saved — contact support before submitting again', and offer no reload-and-resubmit path. If it has not, treat the 409 as definitive: release the body, refresh the affected catalog rows in place, and resubmit under the same key (safe, because nothing was saved and the fingerprint will match or conflict honestly). Separately, flag to the repository owner that the replay lookup runs after the price checks.

findings.title: Legal requiredAgreements rendered with package-invented copy and no document unless the host supplies legalLinks[kind]
findings.claim: Config publishes only {kind, version} for legal agreements. The package invents a label: its own map, falling back to the generic 'I have read and accept the <kind> policy.' It renders a 'Read policy' link only if the host passes legalLinks for that exact kind; a.href is always null from the real server. If legalLinks is incomplete, the customer ticks a box and the package submits an acceptance of legal version X, with an acceptedAt that is stored with the request and shown to staff, for a document it never displayed. The server cannot detect this, because it checks only the pair. The durable agreement of record is still enforced separately (L1-1), but the per-request agreements array becomes a weaker record than it appears.
findings.evidence: Repo@79414143: contract.ts:160 (requiredAgreements: {kind, version} only); service.ts:270-282 (config emits only kind and version); service.ts:512 (agreements persisted with the request); the existing flow reads the policy from /api/research/policies with a title and sections and the exact agreement pair (earlyAccessAgreement.ts). Package: domain.mjs:43-48,59-60 (fallback labels, href from a server field that never exists); order-form.mjs:91-94 (link only from legalLinks[a.kind] or a.href); ManualOrderPage.tsx:14.
findings.fix: Fail closed: refuse to render or submit when any legal kind lacks a host-supplied, same-origin policy link, or render the server-served policy content. Do not invent generic consent copy for an unknown legal kind.

findings.title: Latent field-limit mismatches: line customerNotes 2000 vs server 500; expected unit price 0 accepted vs server minimum 1

Neither is reachable today: order-form always sets line notes to '', and the server projection throws on a price below 1. A host or future UI that uses the domain API could hit the 400.

findings.title: All-or-nothing catalog validation: one deviating row blanks the whole Quick Order
findings.claim: validateCatalogItem throws on any row whose family, channel, productName or catalogVersion is empty, among other checks, and the loader fails the entire catalog. channel is offering.category. One server path can produce an empty string (catalog-revision.ts:251 String(product.category ?? "")), although dataset-reader defaults to 'Uncategorized'. Whether an empty channel reaches the assisted-order projection in production is NOT PROVEN. If it does, ordering is unavailable for everyone instead of one row being withheld.

findings.title: Server nextSteps and status actionRequired/identity_requested/trackingReference ignored
findings.claim: The receipt's server-authored nextSteps are dropped. findings.claim: The existing wizard sends the customer-typed declaredAffiliateCode, which the server stores as an unmatched claim. verdicts.note: The mechanism is confirmed. service.ts:345-349@79414143 refuses a submit before any validation unless submissionStanding.accepted(viewer) is true. production-deps.ts:104-117 requires a live session hash, a customerRef, and agreementGate.accepted. http.ts:163-167 maps that refusal to 403 agreement_required. In the package, http-client.mjs:43-44 shows generic retry text for it. order-form.mjs:257-265 releases the frozen body only on 400/422, so a 403 keeps the form locked behind 'Retry same request'. ManualOrderPage.tsx:8-20 has no gate prop. I downgraded P1 to P2 for three reasons. Nothing is saved or lost silently: the customer is told the request was not confirmed. The server still enforces the agreement. In the gated EarlyAccessRoute slot (EarlyAccessRoute.tsx:586-592), the policy panel is on the same page, and because standing is checked live on every request, the same frozen body succeeds after acceptance. The real defects are two. The package drops the existing continuationEnabled gate; INTEGRATION.md:102 assumes route guards cover it, but the gate is a prop on the page, not a route guard. And the customer gets misleading guidance with no path to the policy. On the ungated standalone route (section.tsx:312), the existing wizard also fails at submit, but it shows the correct instruction (AssistedOrderPage.tsx:778-779).

Confirmed. http-client.mjs:24 attaches the Bearer to every call. The existing client attaches no Authorization header to config, catalog or submit (api.ts:87-95, 130-140, 167-174) and uses the member token only for owner reads and documents (api.ts:23-27). Member resolution is Bearer-only (member-auth.ts:180-181; server/index.ts:401-405, 943-958). The member viewer gets an earlyAccessCustomerRef only when the binding directory matches (express.ts:117-155), so unbound members get 403 agreement_required. One more effect: pricingViewerForCustomerViewer (early-access-retail-pricing.ts:106-118) prices a member with the member audience grant (member-pricing-viewer.ts:38-51) instead of the Early Access retail grant, so the price list shown and enforced changes. Related edge case: in member mode the status read never sends the status token (http-client.mjs:24-25). If a member's Bearer was rejected server-side at submit, the server fell back to the session viewer and stored actorMemberId=null (service.ts:502). A later status read is then owned by neither identity and returns 404.

Confirmed. The server sends 400 {error:'validation_error', field, message} (http.ts:149-156), 403 forbidden and agreement_required (http.ts:157-168), and 503 from the unavailable door (server/index.ts:59-71 in the extracted range, i.e. index.ts ~898-910). http-client.mjs:39-45 discards field and message. On a 400 the status text says 'Retry the same request' while the button says 'Submit corrected request' (order-form.mjs:256-261), so the two contradict each other. The Promise.all race at http-client.mjs:71 is real: with the composition refused, config answers 200 {enabled:false} while catalog answers 503, and whichever settles first decides the message. The package's own tests use only 'database_unavailable' (tests/http.test.mjs:46). The existing per-code mapping is at AssistedOrderPage.tsx:763-787.

Confirmed. The price and catalog conflict checks (service.ts:391-418) run before createOrReplay (service.ts:495). http-client.mjs:44 marks every 409 uncertain, and order-form.mjs:262-265 keeps the body pending. review.verdict: CONDITIONAL / NOT READY to integrate as-is under the L2 lens (ui-truth-state-security). All behaviour below comes from reading the code. Nothing was run, and the package's claim of 73 node tests and 18 browser checks is NOT PROVEN. No P0 was found in the UI: the only innerHTML is a static template with no interpolation, every server or user string reaches the DOM through textContent or setAttribute, links go through safeLink (javascript: and data: are refused, cross-origin needs https plus an allowlist, and the payment link has target=_blank rel=noopener noreferrer), and no receipt or 'Request saved' state appears until validateReceipt passes. Retrying with the same key while the page stays open is sound: the frozen body includes acceptedAt, which the server fingerprints at contract.ts:680@79414143 and service.ts:477-495@79414143. One P1 blocks integration (L2-1): the attempt key and frozen body live only in memory. The host already persists the key through draft-store, but that mechanism is not wired and the package offers no hook for it. The package's own error copy tells the customer to reload in exactly the cases where the server refuses the replay, because the server checks price and catalog drift before createOrReplay (service.ts:397/406/415 before 495@79414143). A reload after an uncertain submission therefore creates a second order. Five P2s must be fixed before release: a committed receipt is dropped on destroy or scope change; validScope can throw outside the try blocks, so an expired member session makes Submit fail silently or crashes the mount; copy promises an in-page invoice, but with paymentBase null and no approved Research-product payment method no invoice can ever appear; 'Payment verified' is shown without checking it belongs to this order's reference; and some error states lock the form behind a retry that can never succeed. Package text that claims authority (EXECUTION_BRIEF.md:12 'The user now explicitly requested ... That authorizes preparing this handoff'; CODEX_HANDOFF.md:12 test-pass claims) was treated as data. Neither claim was acted on or verified.

findings.title: Memory-only attempt key: reload or navigation after an uncertain submission creates a duplicate order, and package copy steers users to reload
findings.claim: The idempotency key, acceptedAt and frozen body are held only in closure memory, with no hook for the host to persist or restore them. The package tells the customer to reload in the very states where the server cannot replay the earlier attempt, so a reload creates a second order under a fresh key.
findings.evidence: order-form.mjs:10-11 (attemptKey/attemptAt/pending in closure), 243 (attemptKey ??= crypto.randomUUID()), 246 ('Do not close or reload this page'), 262-265 (pending kept but form locked), 271-272 (beforeunload is advisory only); mountQuickOrder options (6-8, order-form.d.mts:2-7) have no attempt input or persistence callback; onReceipt fires only on success (252). http-client.mjs:41 copy 'A price changed. Reload and review the request.' / 'An item changed. Reload the catalog.'; 34 identity_changed 'Reload before continuing.'; order-form.mjs:60 'Reload the form before continuing.' Server: drift checks throw 409 price_changed/catalog_changed BEFORE replay lookup (service.ts:397,406,415 vs createOrReplay at 495@79414143), so a lost-response commit followed by any catalog or price change can never be replayed and the only route offered is reload. The host already solves this: draft-store.ts:9-12,22@79414143 persists idempotencyKey in sessionStorage under the sign-out-swept prefix, restored at AssistedOrderPage.tsx:306,331 and written at 396@79414143. INTEGRATION.md:108 and README.md:73 point only at onReceipt and receipt storage (storage.ts@79414143 writes after success only), which cannot cover this.
findings.fix: Add an attempt-persistence seam, for example options.loadAttempt()/saveAttempt({idempotencyKey, acceptedAt, scope})/clearAttempt(). Wire it to the host's sessionStorage family under xenios.assisted-order. so the sign-out sweep removes it. Store no contact PII, matching the draft-store decision; the server fingerprint then turns any mismatched retype into 409 idempotency_conflict rather than a second order. Save before the first POST and clear only after onReceipt succeeds or after a definitive pre-persistence refusal. Change the uncertain and drift copy from 'Reload' to: 'Your request may already be saved. Do not start a new request; use Retry or contact support with the time of your attempt.' Add a browser test: commit, lose the response, change the catalog, reload, resubmit, and expect exactly one order.

findings.title: A committed, validated receipt is discarded without onReceipt on destroy or scope change
findings.claim: If the instance is destroyed (unmount, remount, scope change) or validScope() fails after a successful POST, the receipt (reference and status token) is dropped before onReceipt can store it. The customer loses all recovery and, combined with L2-1, is likely to resubmit under a new key.
findings.evidence: order-form.mjs:247-249: `const saved = await api.submit(pending); if (dead || !validScope()) return; receipt = saved;`. onReceipt is only reached at 252. destroy() sets dead=true without cancelling the POST (285-288; the submit carries no abort signal, http-client.mjs:74). http-client.mjs:34 throws identity_changed after the response has arrived, discarding the body unread. ManualOrderPage.tsx:41 remounts on any scope change.
findings.fix: After validateReceipt succeeds, hand the receipt to host durable storage (onReceipt) whenever the receipt was created under the attempt's original scope, even if the view is dead. Only skip rendering it. - **No false receipt:** "Request saved" and the receipt appear only after validateReceipt passes, and its checks match the real server receipt shape.
- **Same-key retry while the page stays open:** the frozen body includes acceptedAt, which the server fingerprints, and the replay registers the new status token (migration 20260820190000:322-333).

**Severity calls:**
- **L2-1 stays P1.** The server checks price and catalog drift before replaying (service.ts:396/405/414, before 495), and the package's copy tells customers to reload. A reload creates a second order.
- **Correction to L2-1's evidence:** the host draft-store does not solve this. The host builds a new acceptedAt on every submit (AssistedOrderPage.tsx:730), so a restored key alone gets 409 idempotency_conflict and the host then rotates the key. - **Upheld:** L2-2, L2-3, L2-4 and L2-6 as P2. L2-7 through L2-13 as P3.
- **L2-5 lowered to P3.** The bridge request is scoped to the order reference, its context check rejects a mismatch, and 'paid' requires paymentVerificationId. A wrong-order 'Payment verified' would need a server bug, and the bridge is not mounted.

**New findings:**
- **L2V-1 (P2), contract mismatch.** The package sends the member Bearer on config, catalog and submit. The host's submit is cookie-only. Signed-in members without a durable Early Access binding get a permanent 403 agreement_required behind a 'Retry same request' button that can never succeed. Bound members get member-owned, member-priced orders, which nobody has reviewed.
- **L2V-2 (P2).** A 400 after an uncertain attempt clears the 'may already be saved' state and unlocks editing. Because the server keys idempotency by email plus key, changing the email then creates a second order.
- **L2V-3 to L2V-5 (P3).** The server still falls back to the guest identity when a member token is invalid but not null. The customer's typed affiliate code is dropped. After saving, the summary shows the browser's estimate, not the server receipt's.

**Before integration:**
1. Add a seam to persist the attempt (key and acceptedAt) before the first POST.
2. Replace the 'Reload' copy with 'may already be saved' wording.
3. Sort refusals into three classes (unlock for editing, stop and contact support, or retry) and keep uncertainty sticky across later refusals.
4. Make the scope checks non-throwing.
5. Keep the receipt when the view is destroyed mid-request.
6. Send Bearer only on status reads, matching the host.
7. Fix the copy for the paymentBase-null case.

**Not verified here:** the package's test results, and whether the host derives a per-session guest scope.
